messages.author: ba044aa0981678c8
messages.subject: mshape for one landmark configuration
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to write a script for calculating mean landmark
configurations for species. I am using the mshape function to calculate
means. However, it seems that if you use the mshape function to
calculate the mean of a single landmark configuration then it returns an
incorrect result. The reason for using mshape for one landmark
configuration is to automate species mean calculation for situations
where there is only one specimen for one of the species in the dataset.

Here is an example to show the results we get:

require(geomorph)
data(plethodon)
p.gpa<-gpagen(plethodon$land)
# Calculate mean lm config for first two specimens
mshape(p.gpa$coords[,,1:2])
# Calculate mean lm config for first specimen
mshape(p.gpa$coords[,,1])
# This gives 1 x 2 array with coordinates ~1e-17, rather than 12 x 2 array

# Count number of species
p.sp.list <- levels(factor(plethodon$species))
# Create temporary landmark array to place species means into
p.sp.coords.means <- p.gpa$coords[,,1:length(p.sp.list)]

# Calculate mean lm configuration for each species using loop
for (i in 1:length(p.sp.list)) {
p.sp.coords.means[,,i] <- mshape(p.gpa$coords[,,plethodon$species ==
p.sp.list[i]])
}
# This correctly gives mean lm config for 2 species

# Create third species "New" that has only one specimen
p.sp3 <- plethodon$species
levels(p.sp3) <- c(levels(factor(plethodon$species)), c("New"))
p.sp3[1] <- "New"
p.sp3.list <- levels(factor(p.sp3))

# Create temporary landmark array to place species means into
p.sp3.coords.means <- p.gpa$coords[,,1:length(p.sp3.list)]

# Calculate mean lm configuration for three species
for (i in 1:length(p.sp3.list)) {
p.sp3.coords.means[,,i] <- mshape(p.gpa$coords[,,p.sp3 == p.sp3.list[i]])
}
# The third species mean is 1e-17 for all landmarks and dimensions


There may be a much more efficient way of calculating species means
without using a loop, so I would be very grateful for suggestions for
that. However, the mshape appears to give an incorrect result even
without the loop.

If anyone has suggestions for what I might be doing wrong please let me
know.

Thanks,
Al

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] mshape for one landmark configuration
parts:
Al,

You do not need to have such a complicated script. Check out the help file for coords.subset, which has an example for getting group means, and will calculate the mean of one configuration (at least in the most recent version of geomorph on Github, which is what I used to verify).

Best,
Mike

parts:
Mike,

Thanks! I didn't know about the coords.subset function, but that does
work with mshape and lapply.

Continuing from my previous example:

p.sp3.coords <- coords.subset(A = p.gpa$coords, group = p.sp3)
p.sp3.coords.means1 <- lapply(p.sp3.coords, mshape)
plotTangentSpace(p.sp3.coords.means1) # needs 3D array


However, the output from that procedure gives a list of 2D arrays. What
is the easiest way to convert this to a format that can be used by
plotTangentSpace? I tried to use arrayspecs as the message suggests, but
presumably it needs to be converted to a matrix first and I'm having
difficulty doing that keeping the x,y,z dimensions sorted correctly.
Also, it would be good to keep the dimnames (species names) from the
mshape object in the final landmark file.

Cheers,
Al

Hi Mike,

Thanks very much! That worked for this dataset when using 'sapply' and
the 'simplify = "array"' option, if anyone else wants to do this:

p.sp3.coords.means <- sapply(p.sp3.coords, mshape, simplify = "array")

I expected that plotTangentSpace would need a list of 2D arrays, but the
3D array works just as well, which is great.

Cheers,
Al

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] mshape for one landmark configuration
parts:
Dear geomorph community,

Based on this thread, I have updated the mshape function to distinguish between two matrices: one that is a single specimen and one that is an n x pk matrix, where rows are specimens and columns are coordinates; i.e., 1x, 1y, 1z, 2x, 2y, 2z, …

This was possible by checking the dimensions of the matrix. If a matrix (specifically, a 2D array) comprises the data and the number of columns is 2 or 3, it is assumed that this is a single specimen and mshape returns the coordinates of the one specimen. (It is possible that somebody digitized exactly one point for multiple specimens, and then arranged the data into a matrix instead of a 3D array, but we will have to risk this as a rare exception… and/or question the logic.) If a matrix has more than 3 columns, and it can be assumed specimens are rows, then the function returns column means.

The update is currently made to the Github version of geomorph. For multiple specimen arrays, you should notice no change to the function. This should alleviate any sorting issues that cull a data set into a single specimen, when finding means by groups.

Thanks to Murat Maga for pointing out a logical redundancy in our code!

Cheers!
Mike
